claim: Most metabolites are hard to detect in small numbers of cells.
source: Little is known about the metabolic regulation of rare cell populations because most metabolites are hard to detect in small numbers of cells.
evidence: This is stated as background context in the abstract without specific supporting data in this manuscript.

claim: A previous method for metabolomic profiling of flow cytometrically isolated hematopoietic stem cells detected 60 metabolites in 10,000 cells.
source: We previously described a method for metabolomic profiling of flow cytometrically isolated hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that detects 60 metabolites in 10,000 cells (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work (Agathocleous et al., 2017).

claim: The new method detected 160 metabolites in 10,000 HSCs.
source: Here we describe a new method involving hydrophilic liquid interaction chromatography and high-sensitivity orbitrap mass spectrometry that detected 160 metabolites in 10,000 HSCs, including many more glycolytic and lipid intermediates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing metabolite detection in HSCs.

claim: The new method detected many more glycolytic and lipid intermediates than the previous method.
source: Here we describe a new method involving hydrophilic liquid interaction chromatography and high-sensitivity orbitrap mass spectrometry that detected 160 metabolites in 10,000 HSCs, including many more glycolytic and lipid intermediates.
evidence: This is supported by comparison data shown in Figure 4B and throughout the results.

claim: Most metabolite levels did not significantly change during cell isolation.
source: Most metabolite levels did not significantly change during cell isolation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1L-P showing metabolite stability over time.

claim: Mouse HSCs exhibited increased glycerophospholipids relative to bone marrow cells.
source: Mouse HSCs exhibited increased glycerophospholipids relative to bone marrow cells and methotrexate treatment altered purine biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Methotrexate treatment altered purine biosynthesis in HSCs.
source: Mouse HSCs exhibited increased glycerophospholipids relative to bone marrow cells and methotrexate treatment altered purine biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 3F showing AICAR levels increased 88-fold after methotrexate treatment.

claim: Circulating human melanoma cells were depleted for purine intermediates relative to subcutaneous tumors.
source: Circulating human melanoma cells were depleted for purine intermediates relative to subcutaneous tumors, suggesting decreased purine synthesis during metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 3H-K.

claim: Decreased purine synthesis may occur during melanoma metastasis.
source: Circulating human melanoma cells were depleted for purine intermediates relative to subcutaneous tumors, suggesting decreased purine synthesis during metastasis.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation of the observed purine depletion data.

claim: Metabolomics is typically performed using millions of cells.
source: Metabolomics is typically performed using millions of cells, often using cultured cells, whole tissues, or tumor specimens (Jang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Traditional metabolomics measures average metabolite levels across cells in a specimen but is blind to metabolic differences among cells in the same sample.
source: This measures average metabolite levels across the cells in a specimen but is blind to metabolic differences among cells in the same sample.
evidence: This is stated as a logical consequence of bulk analysis methods.

claim: There are limited insights into metabolic heterogeneity among cells within tissues or tumors.
source: As a result, we have limited insights into metabolic heterogeneity among cells within tissues or tumors (Kim and DeBerardinis, 2019; Muir et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review literature.

claim: It is extremely difficult to isolate a million cells from a rare cell population by flow cytometry.
source: It is extremely difficult to isolate a million cells from a rare cell population by flow cytometry.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge based on practical limitations.

claim: One study isolated over 1 million HSCs by flow cytometry but required pooling bone marrow cells from 120 mice.
source: One study isolated over 1 million CD34-Flt3-Lineage-Sca-1+c-kit+ hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) by flow cytometry but pooled bone marrow cells from 120 mice to do it, precluding the analysis of multiple replicates or routine application of this approach (Takubo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Pooling bone marrow from 120 mice precludes the analysis of multiple replicates or routine application.
source: One study isolated over 1 million CD34-Flt3-Lineage-Sca-1+c-kit+ hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) by flow cytometry but pooled bone marrow cells from 120 mice to do it, precluding the analysis of multiple replicates or routine application of this approach (Takubo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the practical limitations of the cited approach.

claim: Metabolomics has been performed on hundreds of thousands of flow cytometrically isolated LSK cells.
source: Metabolomics has also been performed on hundreds of thousands of flow cytometrically isolated Lineage-Sca-1+c-kit+ (LSK) cells (Naka et al., 2015; Karigane et al., 2016), a more heterogeneous population of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: LSK cells are a more heterogeneous population of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
source: Metabolomics has also been performed on hundreds of thousands of flow cytometrically isolated Lineage-Sca-1+c-kit+ (LSK) cells (Naka et al., 2015; Karigane et al., 2016), a more heterogeneous population of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about LSK cell composition.

claim: Only a small minority of LSK cells are HSCs.
source: Since only a small minority of these cells are HSCs, this strategy provides limited insights into metabolite levels in HSCs themselves.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about LSK cell composition.

claim: Metabolomics of LSK cells provides limited insights into metabolite levels in HSCs themselves.
source: Since only a small minority of these cells are HSCs, this strategy provides limited insights into metabolite levels in HSCs themselves.
evidence: This is an inference based on the heterogeneous composition of LSK cells.

claim: Metabolites have been profiled in single cells.
source: Metabolites have been profiled in single cells (Evers et al., 2019; Comi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Single cell metabolomics studies often use very large cells like Xenopus eggs or Aplysia neurons.
source: However, these studies often use very large cells like Xenopus eggs (Onjiko et al., 2015) or Aplysia neurons (Nemes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: Other single cell analyses have focused on small numbers of metabolites or specific subsets of metabolites.
source: Other single cell analyses have focused on small numbers of metabolites or specific subsets of metabolites (Luo and Li, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review.

claim: Single cell metabolomics methods often involve mass spectrometry without chromatographic separation.
source: Single cell metabolomics methods often involve mass spectrometry without chromatographic separation, making it more difficult to identify the detected species (Duncan et al., 2019; Ali et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Mass spectrometry without chromatographic separation makes it more difficult to identify detected species.
source: Single cell metabolomics methods often involve mass spectrometry without chromatographic separation, making it more difficult to identify the detected species (Duncan et al., 2019; Ali et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about analytical limitations.

claim: A previous method detected approximately 60 metabolites in 10,000 flow cytometrically isolated HSCs.
source: We recently described a method for metabolomic analysis of highly purified, flow cytometrically isolated CD150+CD48-LSK HSCs that detected approximately 60 metabolites in 10,000 cells (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: In the previous method, cells were kept cold during the entire purification process.
source: Cells were kept cold during the entire purification process and sorted directly into 80% methanol to immediately quench enzymatic activity and extract metabolites.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the prior study.

claim: In the previous method, cells were sorted directly into 80% methanol to immediately quench enzymatic activity and extract metabolites.
source: Cells were kept cold during the entire purification process and sorted directly into 80% methanol to immediately quench enzymatic activity and extract metabolites.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the prior study.

claim: The previous method revealed that HSCs take up more ascorbate than other hematopoietic cells.
source: This method revealed that HSCs take up more ascorbate than other hematopoietic cells and depend upon ascorbate for epigenetic regulation and leukemia suppression, though coverage of many metabolic pathways was limited.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the prior study (Agathocleous et al., 2017).

claim: HSCs depend upon ascorbate for epigenetic regulation and leukemia suppression.
source: This method revealed that HSCs take up more ascorbate than other hematopoietic cells and depend upon ascorbate for epigenetic regulation and leukemia suppression, though coverage of many metabolic pathways was limited.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the prior study (Agathocleous et al., 2017).

claim: The previous method had limited coverage of many metabolic pathways.
source: This method revealed that HSCs take up more ascorbate than other hematopoietic cells and depend upon ascorbate for epigenetic regulation and leukemia suppression, though coverage of many metabolic pathways was limited.
evidence: This is an assessment of the limitations of the prior method.

claim: Many tumors spontaneously shed cancer cells into the blood.
source: Many tumors spontaneously shed cancer cells into the blood (Micalizzi et al., 2017) but these cells are extremely rare, limiting the amount of material for analysis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Circulating cancer cells are extremely rare, limiting the amount of material for analysis.
source: Many tumors spontaneously shed cancer cells into the blood (Micalizzi et al., 2017) but these cells are extremely rare, limiting the amount of material for analysis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about circulating tumor cells.

claim: Methods have been developed for the flow cytometric isolation and characterization of circulating human melanoma cells from the blood of xenografted mice.
source: We have developed methods for the flow cytometric isolation and characterization of circulating human melanoma cells from the blood of xenografted mice (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: Circulating melanoma cells undergo reversible metabolic changes during metastasis to survive oxidative stress.
source: These cells undergo reversible metabolic changes during metastasis to survive oxidative stress, but these changes are just beginning to be characterized.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020).

claim: The metabolic changes in circulating melanoma cells are just beginning to be characterized.
source: These cells undergo reversible metabolic changes during metastasis to survive oxidative stress, but these changes are just beginning to be characterized.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Mass spectrometric analysis of single circulating cancer cells from patient blood revealed metabolites that differed among various kinds of cancer cells.
source: Mass spectrometric analysis of single circulating cancer cells from the blood of patients revealed metabolites that differed among various kinds of cancer cells (Hiyama et al., 2015; Abouleila et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Fluorescent probes have been used to characterize metabolism in circulating cancer cells.
source: Fluorescent probes have also been used to characterize metabolism in circulating cancer cells (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: The new method increased the number of metabolites detected in 10,000 HSCs to approximately 160.
source: Here we present a new method for the metabolomic analysis of rare stem cell and cancer cell populations isolated by flow cytometry. We have increased the number of metabolites we can detect in 10,000 HSCs to approximately 160.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 4B.

claim: Using the new method, the levels of most metabolites did not significantly change during cell preparation and sorting.
source: Using this method, the levels of most metabolites did not significantly change during cell preparation and sorting.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1H-P.

claim: A key limitation in detecting metabolites in small numbers of cells is discriminating low levels of metabolites from background signals.
source: A key limitation is discriminating the low levels of metabolites present in small numbers of cells from background signals.
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge based on analytical chemistry principles.

claim: Background reflects contamination from various sources and co-association of salts with organic compounds in mass spectrometers to generate matrix ions.
source: Background reflects contamination from various sources as well as the co-association of salts with organic compounds in mass spectrometers to generate organic salt clusters (matrix ions) that obscure the detection of metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about sources of background in mass spectrometry.

claim: The signal to noise ratio in low abundance samples can be improved by transitioning to a mass spectrometer with higher mass resolving power.
source: We reasoned we could improve the signal to noise ratio in low abundance samples and reduce interference by matrix ions by transitioning to a mass spectrometer with higher mass resolving power.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that was tested and supported by the experimental results.

claim: The Q-Exactive HF-X orbitrap mass spectrometer offers four advantages over the triple-quadrupole mass spectrometer used in the previous method.
source: We chose a Q-Exactive HF-X hybrid quadrupole-orbitrap mass spectrometer (ThermoScientific) because it offers four advantages over the triple-quadrupole mass spectrometer used in our previous method (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the detailed explanation of advantages that follows in the text.

claim: The orbitrap instrument captures spectra for the full mass range (80–1200 Daltons) with each scan, greatly increasing the number of metabolites detected.
source: First, whereas the triple-quadrupole instrument acquires data for a predetermined number of metabolites, the orbitrap instrument captures spectra for the full mass range (80–1200 Daltons) with each scan, greatly increasing the number of metabolites detected.
evidence: This is stated as a technical advantage of the orbitrap instrument.

claim: Orbitrap mass analyzers have higher mass resolving power and higher mass accuracy than triple-quadrupole instruments.
source: Second, orbitrap mass analyzers have higher mass resolving power and higher mass accuracy, increasing the ability to discriminate relevant analytes from background ions.
evidence: This is stated as a technical advantage of orbitrap instruments.

claim: Higher mass resolving power and mass accuracy increase the ability to discriminate relevant analytes from background ions.
source: Second, orbitrap mass analyzers have higher mass resolving power and higher mass accuracy, increasing the ability to discriminate relevant analytes from background ions.
evidence: This is an inference based on analytical chemistry principles.

claim: Orbitrap instruments enable comparison of spectra from experimental samples with annotated spectrum libraries for high-confidence identification of metabolites through untargeted acquisition of product ion spectra.
source: Third, through untargeted acquisition of product ion spectra, orbitrap instruments enable the comparison of spectra from experimental samples with annotated spectrum libraries for high-confidence identification of metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as a technical capability of orbitrap instruments.

claim: The HF-X front end optics increase the number of ions that can pass into the mass spectrometer, boosting the signal from low abundance analytes.
source: Finally, compared to other orbitrap models, the HF-X front end optics increase the number of ions that can pass into the mass spectrometer, boosting the signal from low abundance analytes.
evidence: This is stated as a technical advantage of the HF-X model.

claim: HILIC improved the separation of polar metabolites compared to reverse phase chromatography.
source: Polar analytes eluted from the reverse phase column between 3 and 5 min, and from the HILIC column between 2 and 15 min, indicating that HILIC improved polar metabolite separation (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations of elution times.

claim: HILIC yielded more high confidence identifications of metabolites via spectral database matching than reverse phase chromatography.
source: However, the improved metabolite separation and peak quality we observed with HILIC yielded more high confidence identifications of metabolites via spectral database matching alone (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: HILIC enabled the detection of early-eluting lipid metabolites that were not detected using reverse phase chromatography.
source: HILIC also enabled the detection of early-eluting lipid metabolites, which were not detected using reverse phase chromatography.
evidence: This is supported by chromatographic data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Early-eluting lipid metabolites detected by HILIC were well-resolved chromatographically.
source: They were well-resolved chromatographically (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D) and were detected within the linear range of the mass spectrometer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Early-eluting lipid metabolites were detected within the linear range of the mass spectrometer.
source: They were well-resolved chromatographically (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D) and were detected within the linear range of the mass spectrometer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This is supported by standard curve data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–H.

claim: HILIC eliminated the requirement for sample drying.
source: Finally, HILIC eliminated the requirement for sample drying, which can alter the levels of certain metabolites and increase contamination (Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of HILIC with citation support for the problems with drying.

claim: Sample drying can alter the levels of certain metabolites and increase contamination.
source: Finally, HILIC eliminated the requirement for sample drying, which can alter the levels of certain metabolites and increase contamination (Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Background signals arose from the staining medium, flow cytometer sheath fluid, solvent used to extract metabolites, and drying/reconstitution of samples.
source: Background signals arose from the staining medium in which we suspended the cells, the flow cytometer sheath fluid, the solvent we used to extract metabolites from the sorted cells, and the drying and reconstitution of samples prior to liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry (LC-MS) (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated based on prior experience and citation.

claim: Very low levels of background would be negligible when analyzing high abundance samples but interfere with detecting some metabolites in low abundance samples.
source: While these very low levels of background would be negligible when analyzing high abundance samples, they did interfere with the ability to detect some metabolites in low abundance samples.
evidence: This is an inference based on analytical chemistry principles.

claim: Transitioning to HILIC made it possible to directly inject organic solvents into the column without drying and reconstituting in water.
source: Transitioning to HILIC made it possible to directly inject organic solvents into the column, without drying and reconstituting in water.
evidence: This is stated as a technical advantage of HILIC.

claim: The highest level of background contamination was in samples dried in a standard vacuum concentrator.
source: The highest level of background contamination was in the samples dried in the standard vacuum concentrator (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The lowest background was in samples injected into the column without drying.
source: The lowest background was in the samples injected into the column without drying, suggesting drying increased contamination.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Drying increased contamination in metabolomics samples.
source: The lowest background was in the samples injected into the column without drying, suggesting drying increased contamination.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data in Figure 1B.

claim: More metabolites were detected above background in 10,000 WBM cells when samples were not dried (130 metabolites) compared to drying in a standard vacuum concentrator (98 metabolites) or HEPA-filtered vacuum concentrator (123 metabolites).
source: We detected 98, 123, or 130 metabolites significantly above sheath fluid background (always fold change >2 and false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.05) in the samples dried in a standard vacuum concentrator, a HEPA-filtered vacuum concentrator, or undried, respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Avoiding sample drying was incorporated into the method to detect more metabolites above background in low abundance samples.
source: We thus detected more metabolites above background in low abundance samples if we avoided sample drying and incorporated this approach into the method.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 1C.

claim: Different metabolites require different solvents for extraction.
source: Different metabolites require different solvents for extraction (Rabinowitz and Kimball, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: An average of 317 metabolites were detected in 100,000 WBM cells extracted with 80% acetonitrile.
source: Using HILIC and orbitrap mass spectrometry we detected an average of 317 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% acetonitrile and 266 or 273 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% methanol or 40:40:20 methanol:acetonitrile:water, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 266 metabolites were detected in 100,000 WBM cells extracted with 80% methanol.
source: Using HILIC and orbitrap mass spectrometry we detected an average of 317 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% acetonitrile and 266 or 273 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% methanol or 40:40:20 methanol:acetonitrile:water, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 273 metabolites were detected in 100,000 WBM cells extracted with 40:40:20 methanol:acetonitrile:water.
source: Using HILIC and orbitrap mass spectrometry we detected an average of 317 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% acetonitrile and 266 or 273 metabolites in samples extracted with 80% methanol or 40:40:20 methanol:acetonitrile:water, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 80% acetonitrile yielded metabolites that were not detected using other solvents.
source: While we observed considerable overlap in the metabolites detected using each solvent, 80% acetonitrile yielded a number of metabolites that were not detected using the other solvents (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 80% acetonitrile was selected for further method development based on superior metabolite detection.
source: We thus selected 80% acetonitrile for further method development.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the experimental data in Figure 1D-E.

claim: Ion suppression of metabolite signals can occur due to salt in PBS sheath fluid used for flow cytometric sorting.
source: Ion suppression of metabolite signals can occur as a result of the salt in the phosphate buffered saline (PBS) sheath fluid used for flow cytometric sorting: 1–3 nl of sheath fluid is sorted along with each cell depending on whether a 70 µm or 100 µm nozzle is used.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ion suppression in mass spectrometry.

claim: 1–3 nl of sheath fluid is sorted along with each cell depending on whether a 70 µm or 100 µm nozzle is used.
source: Ion suppression of metabolite signals can occur as a result of the salt in the phosphate buffered saline (PBS) sheath fluid used for flow cytometric sorting: 1–3 nl of sheath fluid is sorted along with each cell depending on whether a 70 µm or 100 µm nozzle is used.
evidence: This is stated as technical information about flow cytometry.

claim: Sorting more cells also sorts more salt.
source: Flow cytometry sheath fluid must contain salt to electrostatically charge droplets for sorting; sorting more cells also sorts more salt.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the principles of flow cytometry.

claim: Sorting with the 70 μm nozzle increased the number of metabolites detected above sheath fluid background compared to the 100 μm nozzle, regardless of PBS concentration.
source: Sorting with the 70 μm nozzle increased the number of metabolites we could detect above sheath fluid background as compared to the 100 μm nozzle, regardless of PBS concentration (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: No significant difference was found in the number of metabolites detected above background using 0.5× PBS (157 ± 2) versus 1.0× PBS (149 ± 9).
source: We found no significant difference in the number of metabolites detected above background using 0.5× (157 ± 2) versus 1.0× (149 ± 9) PBS (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: 18 metabolites significantly differed between samples sorted with 0.5× versus 1× PBS sheath fluid.
source: We found 18 metabolites that significantly differed among samples sorted with 0.5× versus 1× PBS sheath fluid (always fold change >2 and FDR < 0.05; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 2, Supplementary Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data listed in supplementary materials.

claim: Pathway enrichment analysis did not identify any pathways significantly enriched among metabolites that changed between 0.5× and 1× PBS.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis did not identify any pathways that were significantly enriched among the changed metabolites.
evidence: This is a result of statistical pathway analysis.

claim: Differences between 0.5× and 1× PBS are unlikely to be due to hypotonic shock because laminar flow minimizes mixing of cell sample buffer and sheath fluid.
source: It is unlikely that these differences are a consequence of hypotonic shock because the laminar flow within the cytometer minimizes the mixing of the cell sample buffer (1× Hank's Buffered Salt Solution [HBSS]) and the sheath fluid.
evidence: This is an inference based on the physics of flow cytometry.

claim: Cells pass through the flow cytometer in less than a second and are immediately lysed upon sorting into extraction solvent.
source: Cells pass through the flow cytometer in less than a second and are immediately lysed upon sorting into the extraction solvent.
evidence: This is stated as a technical detail of the sorting process.

claim: Differences between 0.5× and 1× PBS are more likely to reflect reduced ion suppression and altered metabolite extraction efficiency.
source: Differences between 0.5× and 1× PBS sheath fluid are more likely to reflect reduced ion suppression in samples sorted with 0.5× PBS and altered metabolite extraction efficiency.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed differences.

claim: 0.5× PBS was selected as the sheath fluid for further method development.
source: We selected 0.5× PBS as the sheath fluid for further method development as we tended to detect somewhat more metabolites and higher levels of some metabolites when using 0.5× PBS.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the experimental results.

claim: The number of metabolites detected above background increased significantly with increasing numbers of cells, from 157 ± 4 metabolites in 10,000 cells to 222 ± 9 metabolites in 100,000 cells.
source: The number of metabolites detected above sheath fluid background increased significantly with increasing numbers of cells, from 157 ± 4 metabolites in 10,000 cells to 222 ± 9 metabolites in 100,000 cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: An average of 155 ± 2 metabolites were detected from 10,000 flow cytometrically sorted WBM cells.
source: In the same experiment, we detected an average of 155 ± 2 metabolites from 10,000 flow cytometrically sorted WBM cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Similar numbers of metabolites were detected in flow cytometrically sorted and unsorted samples.
source: We thus detected similar numbers of metabolites in flow cytometrically sorted and unsorted samples.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of sorted and pipetted samples in Figure 1G.

claim: 143–167 metabolites above background were detected in sorted or pipetted AML and ALL cell samples.
source: We detected 143–167 metabolites above background in each sample.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment comparing sorted and pipetted cells.

claim: Principal component analysis revealed differences between sorted and pipetted AML cells.
source: Principal component analysis revealed differences between sorted and pipetted AML cells (Figure 1H; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 3, Supplementary Table 2) whereas differences among sorted and pipetted ALL cells were subtle (Figure 1H; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 4, Supplementary Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by PCA data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Differences between sorted and pipetted ALL cells were subtle.
source: Principal component analysis revealed differences between sorted and pipetted AML cells (Figure 1H; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 3, Supplementary Table 2) whereas differences among sorted and pipetted ALL cells were subtle (Figure 1H; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 4, Supplementary Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by PCA data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: 43 metabolites significantly differed between sorted and pipetted AML cells.
source: Forty-three metabolites significantly differed between sorted and pipetted AML cells while 19 metabolites differed between sorted and pipetted ALL cells (fold change >2 and FDR < 0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of metabolomics data.

claim: 19 metabolites significantly differed between sorted and pipetted ALL cells.
source: Forty-three metabolites significantly differed between sorted and pipetted AML cells while 19 metabolites differed between sorted and pipetted ALL cells (fold change >2 and FDR < 0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of metabolomics data.

claim: Metabolites that differed between sorted and pipetted AML cells were significantly enriched in 'cysteine and methionine metabolism'.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis revealed that metabolites that differed between sorted and pipetted AML cells were significantly enriched in 'cysteine and methionine metabolism'.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: No pathways were significantly enriched among metabolites that differed between sorted and pipetted ALL cells.
source: No pathways were significantly enriched among metabolites that differed between sorted and pipetted ALL cells.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Among sorted samples, 85 metabolites significantly differed between AML and ALL cells.
source: Among sorted samples, 85 metabolites significantly differed between AML and ALL cells while among pipetted samples, 71 of the same metabolites differed (Figure 1I; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 5, Supplementary Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Among pipetted samples, 71 metabolites significantly differed between AML and ALL cells.
source: Among sorted samples, 85 metabolites significantly differed between AML and ALL cells while among pipetted samples, 71 of the same metabolites differed (Figure 1I; see the list of metabolites in Figure 1—source data 5, Supplementary Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Approximately 84% of metabolites that significantly differed among sorted cells also significantly differed among pipetted cells.
source: Approximately 84% of the metabolites that significantly differed among sorted cells also significantly differed among pipetted cells and 73% of the significant differences among pipetted samples also significantly differed among sorted samples.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the overlap of significant metabolites.

claim: 73% of significant differences among pipetted samples also significantly differed among sorted samples.
source: Approximately 84% of the metabolites that significantly differed among sorted cells also significantly differed among pipetted cells and 73% of the significant differences among pipetted samples also significantly differed among sorted samples.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the overlap of significant metabolites.

claim: Of 14 metabolites that significantly changed in sorted but not pipetted cells, 12 trended in the same direction in both sets of samples.
source: Of the 14 metabolites that significantly changed in sorted but not pipetted cells, 12 trended in the same direction in both sets of samples.
evidence: This is an analysis of the directionality of metabolite changes.

claim: Of 26 metabolites that changed in pipetted but not sorted samples, 19 trended in the same direction in both sets of samples.
source: Of the 26 metabolites that changed in pipetted but not sorted samples, 19 trended in the same direction in both sets of samples.
evidence: This is an analysis of the directionality of metabolite changes.

claim: Most metabolites exhibited similar differences among AML and ALL cells irrespective of whether the cells were sorted.
source: Thus, most metabolites exhibited similar differences among AML and ALL cells irrespective of whether the cells were sorted.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the high overlap and directional consistency of metabolite changes.

claim: The slope of the regression for log2-transformed fold change values between AML and ALL cells in sorted versus pipetted samples was near 1 (y = 0.96 × –0.06).
source: The slope of the regression was near 1 (y = 0.96 × –0.06) and the correlation was strong for most metabolites (Spearman correlation coefficient, r = 0.81).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The correlation between sorted and pipetted samples for all detected metabolites was strong (Spearman correlation coefficient, r = 0.81).
source: The slope of the regression was near 1 (y = 0.96 × –0.06) and the correlation was strong for most metabolites (Spearman correlation coefficient, r = 0.81).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: When restricted to metabolites that significantly differed between sorted AML and ALL cells, the correlation was even stronger (y = 0.95 × – 0.15; r = 0.92).
source: When we restricted the analysis to metabolites that significantly differed between sorted AML and ALL cells (fold change >2, FDR < 0.05), the correlation was even stronger (y = 0.95 × – 0.15; r = 0.92; Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1K.

claim: While the levels of some metabolites did change during sorting, most metabolites strongly correlated in sorted and unsorted samples.
source: While the levels of some metabolites did change during sorting, most metabolites strongly correlated in sorted and unsorted samples.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation analyses in Figure 1J-K.

claim: It typically took up to 2 hr to sort HSCs into acetonitrile, starting from when the mice were killed.
source: It typically took up to 2 hr to sort HSCs into acetonitrile, starting from when the mice were killed.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the experimental timeline.

claim: At all time points from 5 to 240 minutes after killing mice, 170–179 metabolites were detected above sheath fluid background.
source: At all time points, we detected 170–179 metabolites above sheath fluid background (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Relative to samples collected at 5 min, only two metabolites significantly changed in samples collected at 15 min.
source: Relative to the samples collected at 5 min, only two metabolites significantly changed (fold change >2 and FDR < 0.05) in the samples collected at 15 min (Figure 1M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: The number of metabolites that significantly changed increased over time, but most changes occurred by 120 min.
source: The number of metabolites that significantly changed increased over time, but most of the changes occurred by 120 min (Figure 1M; see the list of metabolites that changed over time in Figure 1—source data 6, Supplementary Table 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: The only metabolic pathway significantly enriched among metabolites that changed over time was 'purine metabolism'.
source: The only metabolic pathway that was significantly enriched among metabolites that changed over time was 'purine metabolism' as purines were enriched in samples that incubated longer on ice.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Purines were enriched in samples that incubated longer on ice.
source: The only metabolic pathway that was significantly enriched among metabolites that changed over time was 'purine metabolism' as purines were enriched in samples that incubated longer on ice.
evidence: This is supported by the metabolomics data over time.

claim: Some metabolites did change over time but these represented less than 20% of detected metabolites.
source: Thus, some metabolites did change over time but these represented less than 20% of detected metabolites.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the number of metabolites that changed over time.

claim: For log2-transformed values of all detected metabolites in 5 min versus 120 min samples, the slope of regression was near 1 (y = 0.97 × +0.62) and correlation was strong (r = 0.98).
source: The slope of the regression was near 1 (y = 0.97 × +0.62) and the correlation was strong, r = 0.98.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1N.

claim: For non-transformed values of all detected metabolites in 5 min versus 120 min samples, a similarly high correlation was observed.
source: We also plotted non-transformed values for all detected metabolites in 5 min versus 120 min samples, observing a similarly high correlation (Figure 1O).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1O.

claim: For metabolites with signal intensity <1 × 10^8 in 5 min versus 120 min samples, the slope of regression was near 1 (y = 0.95 × +1.1 × 10^6) and correlation was strong (r = 0.97).
source: Again, the slope of the regression was near 1 (y = 0.95 × +1.1 × 106) and the correlation was strong, r = 0.97.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1P.

claim: Most metabolite intensity values strongly correlated among samples that incubated on ice for different periods of time.
source: Thus, most metabolite intensity values strongly correlated among samples that incubated on ice for different periods of time.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation analyses in Figure 1N-P.

claim: Some metabolic changes may occur within seconds of harvesting a tissue in a way not reflected in the time course experiment.
source: However, some metabolic changes may occur within seconds of harvesting a tissue (Lu et al., 2017) in a way that was not reflected in this experiment as the 5 min time point was the earliest at which a bone marrow cell suspension could be reliably obtained.
evidence: This is a caveat based on citation to prior literature and the limitations of the experimental design.

claim: 150–162 metabolites above background were detected in bone marrow cells isolated from HBSS versus PBS.
source: We detected 150–162 metabolites above background in these samples but only five significantly differed between cells isolated from HBSS versus PBS suspended samples (Figure 1—source data 7, Supplementary Table 6).

claim: Only five metabolites significantly differed between cells isolated from HBSS versus PBS.
source: We detected 150–162 metabolites above background in these samples but only five significantly differed between cells isolated from HBSS versus PBS suspended samples (Figure 1—source data 7, Supplementary Table 6).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Glucose was the metabolite that most differed between HBSS and PBS samples, being substantially enriched in cells isolated from HBSS.
source: The metabolite that most differed between these samples was glucose, which was substantially enriched in cells isolated from HBSS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing HBSS and PBS samples.

claim: Pathway enrichment analysis did not detect any pathways enriched among metabolites that differed between HBSS and PBS samples.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis did not detect any pathways enriched among the metabolites that differed among HBSS and PBS samples.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: The presence of glucose in the cell suspension buffer affected glucose levels in sorted cells but had little effect on levels of other metabolites.
source: Therefore, the presence of glucose in the cell suspension buffer did affect glucose levels in the sorted cells but had little effect on the levels of other metabolites.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of HBSS and PBS samples.

claim: CD48-Lineage-Sca1+c-kit+ cells represent 0.05% of WBM cells.
source: CD48-Lineage-Sca1+c-kit+ cells represent 0.05% of WBM cells and are a very highly enriched for HSCs and MPPs (Oguro et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: CD48-Lineage-Sca1+c-kit+ cells are very highly enriched for HSCs and MPPs.
source: CD48-Lineage-Sca1+c-kit+ cells represent 0.05% of WBM cells and are a very highly enriched for HSCs and MPPs (Oguro et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The metabolite profiles of HSCs and MPPs are extremely similar.
source: The metabolite profiles of HSCs and MPPs are extremely similar (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 160 ± 15 metabolites above sheath fluid background were detected in HSCs/MPPs.
source: We detected 160 ± 15 metabolites above sheath fluid background in HSCs/MPPs and 147 ± 15 in WBM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 147 ± 15 metabolites above sheath fluid background were detected in WBM cells.
source: We detected 160 ± 15 metabolites above sheath fluid background in HSCs/MPPs and 147 ± 15 in WBM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A total of 78 metabolites significantly differed in abundance between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells.
source: A total of 78 metabolites significantly differed in abundance between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells (fold change >2 and FDR < 0.05; the metabolites are listed in Figure 2—source data 2, Supplementary Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of metabolomics data.

claim: Of the 78 metabolites that differed between HSCs/MPPs and WBM, 51 differed by at least 2.5-fold.
source: Of these, 51 differed by at least 2.5-fold (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Of 16 metabolites that Agathocleous et al., 2017 found to significantly differ between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells, 13 also significantly differed in the same direction using the new method.
source: Of the 16 metabolites that Agathocleous et al., 2017 found to significantly differ between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells, 13 also significantly differed, in the same direction, using the new method (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The other three metabolites from Agathocleous et al., 2017 either were not detected using the new method or could not be quantitated accurately due to extraction conditions.
source: The other three metabolites either were not detected using the new method or could not be quantitated accurately due to extraction conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for why some metabolites from the prior study were not replicated.

claim: The new method detected most of the metabolic differences between HSC/MPPs and WBM cells observed by Agathocleous et al., 2017, while also detecting 65 additional differences.
source: Thus, the new method detected most of the metabolic differences between HSC/MPPs and WBM cells observed by Agathocleous et al., 2017, while also detecting 65 additional differences.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison with prior work.

claim: Pathway enrichment analysis found only one pathway significantly enriched (FDR < 0.01): 'glycerophospholipid metabolism'.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis found only one pathway that was significantly enriched (FDR < 0.01): 10 of 36 metabolites in the murine KEGG 'glycerophospholipid metabolism' pathway significantly differed in abundance between HSC/MPPs and WBM cells.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: 10 of 36 metabolites in the murine KEGG 'glycerophospholipid metabolism' pathway significantly differed in abundance between HSC/MPPs and WBM cells.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis found only one pathway that was significantly enriched (FDR < 0.01): 10 of 36 metabolites in the murine KEGG 'glycerophospholipid metabolism' pathway significantly differed in abundance between HSC/MPPs and WBM cells.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: HSCs were enriched for many components of the Kennedy (cytidine diphosphate-choline) pathway.
source: HSCs were enriched for many components of the Kennedy (cytidine diphosphate-choline) pathway (Li and Vance, 2008; Kennedy and Weiss, 1956), including choline, choline phosphate, CDP-choline, ethanolamine phosphate, glycerophosphorylcholine, glycerophosphorylethanolamine, and many phosphatidylcholines (PC), phosphatidylethanolamines (PE), lysophosphatidylcholines (Lyso-PC), and lysophosphatidylethanolamines (Lyso-PE) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Acetylcholine and several phosphatidylserine (PS) species were depleted in HSC/MPPs as compared to WBM.
source: Acetylcholine and several phosphatidylserine (PS) species were depleted in HSC/MPPs as compared to WBM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: These results raise the possibility that glycerophospholipid synthesis is activated in HSC/MPPs relative to WBM.
source: These results raise the possibility that glycerophospholipid synthesis is activated in HSC/MPPs relative to WBM; however, additional studies will be required in the future to test this.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the metabolomics data.

claim: Additional studies will be required to test whether glycerophospholipid synthesis is activated in HSC/MPPs.
source: These results raise the possibility that glycerophospholipid synthesis is activated in HSC/MPPs relative to WBM; however, additional studies will be required in the future to test this.
evidence: This acknowledges the need for future validation studies.

claim: The prominence of phospholipids among differences between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells illustrates the ability of the new method to detect differences not detected by prior methods.
source: The prominence of phospholipids among the differences between HSCs/MPPs and WBM cells illustrates the ability of the new method to detect differences not detected by prior methods.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the improved capabilities of the new method.

claim: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and AICAR transaminase (ATIC), steps in de novo purine biosynthesis.
source: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and AICAR transaminase (ATIC), steps in de novo purine biosynthesis (Baggott et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Methotrexate treatment did not significantly affect bone marrow cellularity.
source: Methotrexate treatment did not significantly affect bone marrow cellularity or the frequencies of HSCs, MPPs, or LSK cells in the bone marrow (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Methotrexate treatment did not significantly affect the frequencies of HSCs, MPPs, or LSK cells in the bone marrow.
source: Methotrexate treatment did not significantly affect bone marrow cellularity or the frequencies of HSCs, MPPs, or LSK cells in the bone marrow (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Methotrexate treatment did not significantly affect the reconstituting potential of WBM cells upon competitive transplantation into irradiated mice.
source: Methotrexate treatment also did not significantly affect the reconstituting potential of WBM cells upon competitive transplantation into irradiated mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The only pathway significantly enriched among metabolites that differed after methotrexate treatment was 'purine metabolism'.
source: Metabolomic analysis of 10,000 HSC/MPPs from the bone marrow of methotrexate-treated and control mice revealed that the only pathway that was significantly enriched among the metabolites that differed was 'purine metabolism'.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Methotrexate would be expected to alter folate metabolism, but folate species are very difficult to detect by metabolomics.
source: While methotrexate would also be expected to alter folate metabolism, folate species are very difficult to detect by metabolomics (Zheng et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2017) and are not detected by our method.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation with citation support.

claim: Folate species are not detected by the method described in this study.
source: While methotrexate would also be expected to alter folate metabolism, folate species are very difficult to detect by metabolomics (Zheng et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2017) and are not detected by our method.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: AICAR levels would be expected to increase after methotrexate treatment given that methotrexate inhibits ATIC.
source: Given that methotrexate inhibits ATIC, AICAR levels would be expected to increase after methotrexate treatment (Cronstein et al., 1993; Baggott et al., 1986; Allegra et al., 1985).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of methotrexate action with citation support.

claim: AICAR levels were 88-fold higher in HSCs/MPPs from methotrexate-treated as compared to control mice.
source: Consistent with this, AICAR levels were 88-fold higher in HSCs/MPPs from methotrexate-treated as compared to control mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The method was capable of detecting expected metabolic perturbations in HSCs in vivo.
source: The method was thus capable of detecting expected metabolic perturbations in HSCs in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the methotrexate experiment results.

claim: When efficiently metastasizing human melanomas are subcutaneously transplanted into NSG mice they spontaneously metastasize, giving rise to rare circulating melanoma cells.
source: When efficiently metastasizing human melanomas are subcutaneously transplanted into NSG mice they spontaneously metastasize, giving rise to rare circulating melanoma cells in the blood, lymph, and metastatic tumors (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020; Ubellacker et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Blood from 6 to 10 mice per sample was pooled to isolate 10,000 circulating melanoma cells.
source: We pooled blood from 6 to 10 mice per sample to isolate 10,000 circulating melanoma cells.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: 145 metabolites above sheath fluid background were detected in subcutaneous tumor melanoma cell samples.
source: We detected 145 and 154 metabolites above sheath fluid background in the subcutaneous tumor and circulating melanoma cell samples, respectively (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: 154 metabolites above sheath fluid background were detected in circulating melanoma cell samples.
source: We detected 145 and 154 metabolites above sheath fluid background in the subcutaneous tumor and circulating melanoma cell samples, respectively (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Pathway enrichment analysis found one pathway that significantly differed (FDR < 0.01) between subcutaneous tumor and circulating melanoma cells: 'purine metabolism'.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis of all metabolites that significantly differed between subcutaneous tumor and circulating melanoma cells (p<0.05) found one pathway that significantly (FDR < 0.01) differed, 'purine metabolism'.
evidence: This is a result of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Several purine biosynthesis intermediates were depleted in circulating melanoma cells as compared to subcutaneous tumors, including IMP, XMP, GMP, and AMP.
source: Several purine biosynthesis intermediates were depleted in circulating melanoma cells as compared to subcutaneous tumors, including insoine monophosphate (IMP), xanthosine monophosphate (XMP), guanosine monophosphate (GMP), and adenosine monophosphate (AMP) (Figure 3H–K; Figure 3—source data 2, Supplementary table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H-K.

claim: Circulating melanoma cells experience high levels of oxidative stress.
source: Given that circulating melanoma cells experience high levels of oxidative stress (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020), these data raise the possibility that metastasizing melanoma cells reduce purine biosynthesis, and perhaps other anabolic pathways, to preserve NADPH for oxidative stress resistance.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The data raise the possibility that metastasizing melanoma cells reduce purine biosynthesis to preserve NADPH for oxidative stress resistance.
source: Given that circulating melanoma cells experience high levels of oxidative stress (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020), these data raise the possibility that metastasizing melanoma cells reduce purine biosynthesis, and perhaps other anabolic pathways, to preserve NADPH for oxidative stress resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the purine depletion data.

claim: Metastasizing melanoma cells may reduce other anabolic pathways to preserve NADPH for oxidative stress resistance.
source: Given that circulating melanoma cells experience high levels of oxidative stress (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020), these data raise the possibility that metastasizing melanoma cells reduce purine biosynthesis, and perhaps other anabolic pathways, to preserve NADPH for oxidative stress resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation extending beyond the purine data.

claim: The new method significantly increased metabolite numbers and pathway coverage relative to the prior method.
source: The method for metabolomic analysis of rare cells described in this study significantly increased metabolite numbers and pathway coverage relative to our prior method (Agathocleous et al., 2017; Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Signal to noise ratio was improved by using HILIC and an orbitrap mass spectrometer.
source: We improved signal to noise ratio by using HILIC and an orbitrap mass spectrometer.
evidence: This is a summary of the methodological improvements.

claim: Contamination was decreased by eliminating sample drying.
source: We decreased contamination by eliminating sample drying and improved chromatographic performance by extracting metabolites with 80% acetonitrile.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1B-C.

claim: Chromatographic performance was improved by extracting metabolites with 80% acetonitrile.
source: We decreased contamination by eliminating sample drying and improved chromatographic performance by extracting metabolites with 80% acetonitrile.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1D-E.

claim: In principle, this method can be used to analyze any cell population isolated by flow cytometry.
source: In principle, this method can be used to analyze any cell population isolated by flow cytometry, though in practice it is most useful when cell numbers are limited and when enzymatic dissociation is not required.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applicability of the method.

claim: In practice, the method is most useful when cell numbers are limited and when enzymatic dissociation is not required.
source: In principle, this method can be used to analyze any cell population isolated by flow cytometry, though in practice it is most useful when cell numbers are limited and when enzymatic dissociation is not required.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical limitations of the method.

claim: Input variation among samples was normalized by ensuring that average signal intensity values of metabolites detected above background were equal in samples being compared.
source: We normalized for input variation among samples by ensuring that the average signal intensity values of metabolites detected above background were equal in the samples being compared.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach for normalization.

claim: It is impractical to include isotopically labeled internal standards within the initial metabolomic analysis since the relative levels of hundreds of different metabolites are assessed.
source: While it is impractical to include isotopically labeled internal standards within the initial metabolomic analysis, since the relative levels of hundreds of different metabolites are assessed, we routinely follow-up metabolomics with other methods optimized to extract and quantitate specific metabolites of interest.
evidence: This is stated as a practical limitation of broad metabolomics approaches.

claim: Follow-up assays include labeled internal standards to determine absolute concentrations of specific metabolites.
source: In those follow-up assays we include labeled internal standards to determine absolute concentrations (Tasdogan et al., 2020; Ubellacker et al., 2020; Piskounova et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as the approach for validation studies with citation support.

claim: Cells can undergo metabolic changes upon removal from their in vivo environment.
source: Cells can undergo metabolic changes upon removal from their in vivo environment (Lau et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Metabolic changes upon cell removal are a particular problem when cells are enzymatically dissociated or sorted into buffers requiring additional processing.
source: This is a particular problem when cells are enzymatically dissociated as they exchange metabolites with the dissociation medium, or when cells are sorted into buffers that require additional processing steps before cell lysis and metabolite extraction (Lau et al., 2020; Binek et al., 2019; Llufrio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: To avoid changes in metabolites during cell processing, cells were worked with quickly and kept cold from the time they left the animal until sorted into acetonitrile.
source: To avoid changes in metabolites during cell processing, we worked quickly and kept the cells cold from the time they left the animal until they were sorted into acetonitrile.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach.

claim: Cellular metabolism is immediately quenched by sorting into cold acetonitrile.
source: Cellular metabolism is immediately quenched by sorting into cold acetonitrile.
evidence: This is stated as a principle of the method.

claim: Most metabolite levels were not significantly changed by cell preparation and sorting, at least beyond 5 min after the mouse was killed.
source: Therefore, most metabolite levels were not significantly changed by cell preparation and sorting, at least beyond 5 min after the mouse was killed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the time course and sorting comparison experiments.

claim: Some metabolite levels might change less than a minute after removal of cells from their normal physiological environment in a way not detected in the experiments.
source: However, some metabolite levels might change less than a minute after the removal of cells from their normal physiological environment in a way that would not have been detected in our experiments (Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a caveat with citation support.

claim: If metabolites change within seconds of cell removal, it will not be possible to quantitate these metabolites in flow cytometrically isolated cells.
source: If so, it will not be possible to quantitate these metabolites in flow cytometrically isolated cells.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of the method.

claim: HILIC reduced ion suppression compared to the prior method because salt eluted after the metabolites of interest.
source: We reduced ion suppression compared to our prior method because salt eluted after the metabolites of interest on HILIC columns (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of HILIC with reference to experimental data.

claim: HILIC enabled the detection of many lipid species in addition to improving separation of polar metabolites.
source: Third, HILIC improved the separation of polar metabolites, such as central carbon metabolites, while also enabling the detection of many lipid species.
evidence: This is supported by the metabolomics data showing lipid detection.

claim: Some metabolites are better resolved and detected by reverse phase chromatography.
source: Nonetheless, some metabolites are better resolved and detected by reverse phase chromatography.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of HILIC.

claim: Adapting this low cell number method to other chromatographies could improve the detection of certain classes of metabolites.
source: Therefore, while HILIC provided a net advantage for our purposes, adapting this low cell number method to other chromatographies could improve the detection of certain classes of metabolites.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future method development.

claim: Prior studies have explored many aspects of metabolomics methods, including extraction solvents and drying.
source: Prior studies have explored many aspects of metabolomics methods, including extraction solvents and drying (Theodoridis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Methanol–water and acetonitrile–water mixtures have been reported to capture more metabolites than other solvents.
source: Methanol–water and acetonitrile–water mixtures have been reported to capture more metabolites than other solvents (Want et al., 2006; Jiye et al., 2005; Bruce et al., 2008; Masson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Methanol is nucleophilic and can degrade metabolites with electrophilic moieties, such as nucleoside phosphates.
source: Methanol is nucleophilic and can degrade metabolites with electrophilic moieties, such as nucleoside phosphates (Rabinowitz and Kimball, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Data quality and accuracy are improved by minimizing sample manipulation after metabolite extraction, including by avoiding drying.
source: Data quality and accuracy are also improved by minimizing sample manipulation after metabolite extraction, including by avoiding drying, which can promote oxidation (Siegel et al., 2014; Fan et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2017; Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Drying can promote oxidation of metabolites.
source: Data quality and accuracy are also improved by minimizing sample manipulation after metabolite extraction, including by avoiding drying, which can promote oxidation (Siegel et al., 2014; Fan et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2017; Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Acetonitrile–water solvent and avoiding drying yielded the highest number of metabolites detected above sheath fluid background.
source: We found that acetonitrile–water solvent and avoiding drying yielded the highest number of metabolites detected above sheath fluid background.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental comparisons.

claim: HILIC resolution of metabolites was improved when samples were injected in acetonitrile–water instead of methanol–water.
source: HILIC resolution of metabolites was also improved when samples were injected in acetonitrile–water instead of methanol–water.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the method development.

claim: The extraction conditions used are not suitable for quantitation of some metabolites, including those that spontaneously oxidize.
source: The extraction conditions we used are not suitable for the quantitation of some metabolites, including those that spontaneously oxidize (Lu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation with citation support.

claim: Ascorbate spontaneously oxidizes upon extraction from cells.
source: For example, ascorbate spontaneously oxidizes upon extraction from cells Washko et al., 1992; therefore, in our prior study we added EDTA to the extraction solvent to prevent spontaneous oxidation (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In the prior study, EDTA was added to the extraction solvent to prevent spontaneous oxidation of ascorbate.
source: For example, ascorbate spontaneously oxidizes upon extraction from cells Washko et al., 1992; therefore, in our prior study we added EDTA to the extraction solvent to prevent spontaneous oxidation (Agathocleous et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the prior study.

claim: EDTA was not added to the extraction solvent in the current study in an effort to devise a general method.
source: In an effort to devise a general method in the current study, we did not add EDTA to the extraction solvent and therefore did not measure ascorbate levels accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological decision.

claim: Ascorbate levels were not measured accurately in the current study.
source: In an effort to devise a general method in the current study, we did not add EDTA to the extraction solvent and therefore did not measure ascorbate levels accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the methodological decision.

claim: Ascorbate was one of three metabolites that differed between HSCs and WBM in the prior study but not detected as different in the current study.
source: Consistent with this, ascorbate was one of the three metabolites that differed between HSCs and WBM cells in our prior study (Agathocleous et al., 2017) that we did not detect as different in the current study (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with prior results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Spermidine and betaine were not detected using the new method.
source: The other two were spermidine and betaine, which were not detected using the new method.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the new method.

claim: Few studies have examined lipid metabolism in HSCs.
source: Few studies have examined lipid metabolism in HSCs (Xie et al., 2019; Ito et al., 2012; Ito et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2018; Pernes et al., 2019), partly because methods have not been readily available to quantitate lipid levels in HSCs.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature with citations.

claim: Methods have not been readily available to quantitate lipid levels in HSCs.
source: Few studies have examined lipid metabolism in HSCs (Xie et al., 2019; Ito et al., 2012; Ito et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2018; Pernes et al., 2019), partly because methods have not been readily available to quantitate lipid levels in HSCs.
evidence: This is stated as a reason for the limited research in this area.

claim: The ability of the new method to detect more than 60 lipids in 10,000 HSCs may facilitate future studies of lipid metabolism in stem cells.
source: The ability of the new method to detect more than 60 lipids in 10,000 HSCs may facilitate future studies of lipid metabolism in stem cells.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential impact of the method.

claim: Cancer cells must undergo metabolic changes to survive oxidative stress during metastasis.
source: Cancer cells must undergo metabolic changes to survive oxidative stress during metastasis (Piskounova et al., 2015; Tasdogan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Better understanding the metabolic changes in metastasizing cancer cells could reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities to block cancer progression.
source: Better understanding the metabolic changes could reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities to block cancer progression.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential clinical implications.
